newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French 10-year bond futures settled higher on Friday, fired by hopes that the row over EU budgetary discipline would be resolved as well as by weaker-than-expected U.S. producer price data.
But some economists and analysts said the market might be overconfident that the "stability pact" would be ratified by EU finance ministers at a summit in Amsterdam next week.

"It's very thin ice the market is skating on. There is a much more serious problem than the rhetoric suggests or than market prices suggest," said Iain Lindsay, senior bond analyst at Credit Lyonnais.

"There was nothing in anything (French Finance Minister Dominique) Strauss-Kahn or (Prime Minister Lionel) Jospin said that suggests they are are going to soften their position. They are sticking to their guns," he said.

French and German leaders made progress but failed to defuse the dispute over French demands for new EU commitments to promote growth and jobs at the Poitiers summit. The EU finance ministers will meet again on Sunday on the eve of the Amsterdam summit to seek a solution. France said it wants the jobs and growth resolution appended to the stability pact but Germany has refused any link between the pact and an EU jobs statement.

The 10-year bond future started higher and extended its gains on the release of U.S. data showing producer prices fell for the fifth straight month in May, dropping by 0.3 percent against expectations of a rise of 0.1 percent.

"There was a lot of short-covering," said Nathalie Fillet of Banque Paribas. She said the market was supported by strong liquidity but there was risk of a correction next week. "It's looking a little expensive at these levels. We've got some uncertainties ahead with the Amsterdam summit and Jospin's speech is likely to contain measures to stimulate consumption which won't be appreciated by the markets," she said.
Statements by French and German leaders at the close of summit reporting progress on the stability pact pushed the 10-bond future to the day's highs. It settled 56 basis points higher at 128.92.
Filet said the bond market appeared to believe a deal to ratify the stability pact was within reach at Amsterdam.

But Eric Chaney, economist at Morgan Stanley, preached caution. "I am skeptical about a formal ratification of the stability pact in Amsterdam. It is not impossible but it is far from being a done deal," he said.

"My impression is the mood (at Poitiers) was not very good," he said. "When (Finance Minister Dominique) Strauss-Kahn said he hoped 80 percent of the issues would be resolved by the (time of the) meeting at Amsterdam, my guess is that the 20 percent remaining is likely to be difficult to resolve," he said..

September three-month PIBOR also was up strongly, rising seven basis points to 96.56. The franc was steady against the mark at 3.3735 per mark but retreated against the dollar. The dollar was trading at 5.5617 francs, its highest level since February 1994.
The cash market outperformed Germany with the negative 10-year OAT-Bund spread widening to minus nine from minus seven.
